observations: The source text of LM2 Torah 58 is four sentences long and contains no bechina (parallel-aspect) equating language whatsoever. The teaching presents one philosophical argument: a tzaddik who achieves the state of 'ayin' (nothingness/self-nullification) transcends fixed location and is therefore present everywhere, enabling him to watch over the world — just as God, infinitely transcendent, exercises particular providence over all creation. The key concepts in the text are: צַדִּיק, אַיִן, יֵשׁ, הַשְׁגָּחָה פְּרָטִית, and מָקוֹם. These concepts relate to each other through causal logic and analogy, not through the symmetric 'shared nature' relationship that defines bechina. Specifically: 'ayin' PRODUCES omnipresence (eitza, cause → effect); God's transcendence is an ANALOGY for the tzaddik's omnipresence (proof by comparison); 'yesh' and 'ayin' are DEFINITIONAL OPPOSITES (antonymous, not bechina-paired). To qualify for a new package, there must be three or more concepts connected by explicit bechina language ('הוּא בְּחִינַת', 'נִקְרָא', 'כַּנַּ"ל') forming an independent domain. This condition is not met. There is not a single bechina formulation in the text. No new packages are warranted.
